events.title: Emperor Justinian I dies
events.description: Justinian died in Constantinople after a 38-year reign. He reconquered North Africa and Italy, codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis and built the Hagia Sophia.
events.html: Justinian died in Constantinople after a 38-year reign. He reconquered North Africa and Italy, codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis and built the Hagia Sophia.

events.title: Moby-Dick is published in New York
events.description: Harper and Brothers published Herman Melville's Moby-Dick, a month after its London edition. Poorly received at first, the tale of Captain Ahab's pursuit of the white whale is now a classic of American literature.
events.html: Harper and Brothers published Herman Melville's Moby-Dick, a month after its London edition. Poorly received at first, the tale of Captain Ahab's pursuit of the white whale is now a classic of American literature.

events.title: Nellie Bly sets out to beat Phileas Fogg's 80 days
events.description: New York World reporter Nellie Bly left Hoboken to travel around the world faster than Jules Verne's fictional hero. She returned in just over 72 days, a world record at the time.
events.html: New York World reporter Nellie Bly left Hoboken to travel around the world faster than Jules Verne's fictional hero. She returned in just over 72 days, a world record at the time.

events.title: The Luftwaffe devastates Coventry
events.description: Some 500 German bombers attacked Coventry overnight, killing about 570 people and destroying the medieval cathedral. It was one of the heaviest raids of the Blitz.

events.title: Apollo 12 launches for the Moon
events.description: Apollo 12 survived two lightning strikes during launch from Cape Kennedy. Five days later Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed precisely beside the Surveyor 3 probe in the Ocean of Storms.
